scan_metadata.llm_overall_assessment: The package is a scientific computing skill for 13C metabolic flux analysis. All code (scripts/mfa.py, scripts/_mfa_model.py, scripts/_mfa_fit.py) performs local JSON input validation, numerical isotope simulation via mfapy, and SciPy-based constrained optimization. There is no network activity at runtime, no file writes outside the user-specified output path (which is explicitly guarded against overwriting inputs), no environment/credential access, no subprocess or shell execution, no eval/exec, and no encoding/obfuscation. The only network usage is the documented installation of pinned public dependencies (mfapy from an immutable Git commit, plus pinned numpy/scipy/nlopt), which is normal dependency installation and is disclosed in the manifest and SKILL.md. Input handling is defensively strict (identifier regex limiting what reaches mfapy's code generator, rejection of non-finite JSON constants, duplicate-key rejection, bounded list sizes). The SKILL.md body contains no instruction overrides, hidden actions, auto-execution triggers, or directions to conceal activity from the user; its documented commands are user-invoked CLI calls. Missing referenced files are a quality/packaging matter, not a security threat. The description is specific and matches the implemented capability, with no discovery-baiting language.

The package contains only two markdown files (SKILL.md and references/api-endpoints.md) and no executable scripts. Content is documentation for the Adaptyv Bio Foundry REST API and Python SDK: endpoint inventory, request/response schemas, lifecycle statuses, pagination/filter syntax, and illustrative Python snippets. Credential handling is conventional and appropriate: the bearer token is read from the ADAPTYV_API_KEY environment variable and sent only as an Authorization header to the documented vendor host (devs.adaptyvbio.com), with explicit cautions to never print or commit tokens, not to forward the Foundry bearer to Stripe on redirects, and never to include tokens in feedback submissions. No hardcoded secrets, no encoded/obfuscated payloads, no download-and-execute chain, no instructions to hide actions from the user, and no instruction overrides. Dependency installation is from the vendor's named official GitHub repository pinned to a specific commit, which is normal supply usage rather than substitution. Automation flags (skip_draft, auto_accept_quote) and payment endpoints are the skill's declared purpose and are explicitly gated on the user's approved budget/purchase scope, with a statement that examples do not execute payment or lab work. The citation section asks the agent to add a reference and to disclose that it did so, which is transparent self-attribution rather than a covert action. Several referenced paths (adaptyv.py, templates/ and assets/ copies of the endpoint reference) are missing, which is a documentation-quality issue, not a security threat.

The 'aeon' skill is a documentation-only package: 12 markdown files (SKILL.md plus references/) with no scripts, binaries, or hidden executables. Content is entirely procedural guidance for the aeon time-series ML library, consisting of API usage examples, algorithm-selection advice, and correct-usage caveats. Installation guidance uses standard registry commands (`uv pip install "aeon==1.6.0"`), which is normal dependency setup for the stated purpose. Network references are limited to the official aeon documentation site, GitHub, Zenodo/timeseriesclassification.com public dataset and benchmark-results endpoints used by aeon's own loaders — all consistent with the declared purpose and disclosed in the manifest compatibility note. No sensitive-file, environment-variable, or credential access appears anywhere; no data is sent to any sink. Declared tools (Read, Write, Edit, Bash) match the documented workflow of writing and running Python analysis code. There are no instruction overrides, no directives to hide actions or skip user confirmation, no automatic pre-flight script execution, no encoded or obfuscated payloads, and no unicode steganography. The closing section asks the agent to cite the skill authors' paper when it materially contributed, but it is conditional, transparent (explicitly requires informing the user), and does not instruct concealment or data transmission, so it does not rise to a security finding. The deterministic pre-scan produced no findings and the package projection is complete, consistent with this assessment.

The alphagenome skill is a legitimate scientific tooling package that wraps DeepMind's official AlphaGenome/Atlas Python SDK. All three scripts (atlas_query.py, score_variants.py, atlas_link.py) plus the shared _common.py perform variant parsing, gRPC queries to the declared endpoint gdmscience.googleapis.com:443, and local table/URL output. The API key is read only from environment variables (ALPHAGENOME_API_KEY / ALPHA_GENOME_API_KEY), never hardcoded, never accepted on the command line, and never written into outputs or transmitted anywhere other than the intended AlphaGenome service via standard x-goog-api-key metadata. There is no shell execution, no subprocess usage, no eval/exec, no download-then-execute chain, no obfuscation or encoded payloads, and no hidden or unreferenced files. Network destinations are limited to documented Google/DeepMind domains (deepmind.google.com portal links, storage.googleapis.com GENCODE annotation, alphagenomedocs.com documentation). The SKILL.md body contains no instruction overrides, no directives to hide actions from the user, and no mandatory pre-flight script execution; the citation request (adding an arXiv reference and telling the user) is disclosed, non-covert, and ordinary academic attribution. Declared allowed-tools (Read, Write, Edit, Bash) are consistent with a CLI-driven analysis skill, and the pre-scan produced zero deterministic findings with full analyzability. No security findings warrant reporting.

The package is a domain-specific analytical method validation skill. All eight Python files use only the Python standard library (argparse, csv, json, math, statistics, pathlib) to perform statistical computations on user-supplied CSV/TSV/JSON files. There are no network calls, no subprocess/os.system/eval/exec usage, no file writes outside explicit user-directed stdout redirection, no environment variable or credential access, and no obfuscated or encoded payloads. Input handling is defensively bounded (MAX_INPUT_BYTES, MAX_ROWS, finite-number validation, explicit InputError exit code 2). The SKILL.md body contains only domain guidance; its documented bash commands invoke the bundled scripts with user-supplied data files and are not auto-executed as hidden pre-flight steps. The declared allowed-tools (Read, Write, Edit, Bash) are consistent with running the bundled scripts and emitting protocol/report Markdown. The optional citation step suggesting an arXiv abstract fetch is a disclosed, user-visible documentation action with no local data sent outward. Several referenced reference/asset files are absent, which is a documentation-completeness issue rather than a security threat. No prompt injection, instruction override, exfiltration sink, or capability-inflation misuse was identified.

The package is a documentation-oriented Agent Skill for the AnnData Python library, consisting entirely of six markdown files (SKILL.md plus reference documents on data structure, I/O, concatenation, manipulation, and best practices). No executable scripts are present, and the deterministic pre-scan produced zero findings. Content is limited to illustrative Python snippets for creating/reading/writing AnnData objects, a standard `uv pip install "anndata==0.13.4"` dependency instruction, and links to official anndata/scverse documentation. The only network-related directive is an optional fetch of a public arXiv record for citation metadata, which does not transmit local data. No instruction overrides, hidden execution triggers, obfuscation, secret access, exfiltration sinks, or capability inflation were observed; the declared tools (Read, Write, Edit, Bash) are consistent with the stated data-format workflow purpose. Several referenced reference/template/asset paths are missing, which is a documentation-quality issue rather than a security threat.

The 'arbor' skill is a research-methodology package that implements Hypothesis Tree Refinement bookkeeping. The bundled scripts/tree.py (SRC:ba71d5918de41e0c) uses only the Python standard library (argparse, json, math, sys, time, pathlib) and performs purely local JSON state management under a .arbor/ directory: creating nodes, recording scores, propagating insights, pruning, and rendering text projections. There is no network access, no subprocess/exec/eval, no file reads outside the run directory, no environment or credential access, and no encoding/obfuscation. The SKILL.md body (SRC:0e95f5a3666031d6) contains no instruction overrides, no directives to hide actions from the user, and no automatic execution of downloaded payloads; all documented commands are explicit, user-visible invocations of the bundled helper. Referenced docs (SRC:8b7cc92786f4c8ac, SRC:c4f7c032cef3d4f5, SRC:91294e70f992dd97, SRC:a93b31a056841660) describe installing the upstream 'arbor-agent' package from PyPI with a pinned version and provider credentials supplied via standard environment variables for the intended service — ordinary, disclosed dependency and auth usage, and the docs explicitly warn that a native run can be paid and is not a dry run. Subagent dispatch, git worktree isolation, and Bash usage match the declared allowed-tools and the skill's stated purpose of orchestrating multi-experiment research runs; budget/cycle limits are documented and the manifest declares its capabilities. Missing optional reference paths under assets/ and templates/ are quality artifacts of path probing, not security issues. The trusted pre-scan reported zero deterministic findings and no unreferenced scripts.

The arboreto skill is a legitimate scientific computing package for gene regulatory network inference. SKILL.md and the three reference markdown files contain only domain documentation (algorithm choice, Dask backend configuration, data contracts, troubleshooting) with pinned dependency installs from PyPI via uv — normal, declared setup for the service the skill provides. The single bundled script (scripts/basic_grn_inference.py) reads a local TSV, validates numeric input, runs GRNBoost2 on a bounded local Dask cluster, and writes a local output TSV; it performs no network I/O, no subprocess/shell execution, no environment or credential access, and no dynamic code evaluation. The remote-scheduler section only documents standard `dask scheduler`/`dask worker` CLI forms with a placeholder hostname and explicitly flags the trust boundary. The citation section asks the agent to optionally fetch a public arXiv record and disclose the added citation to the user — transparent, user-visible, and not data exfiltration or hidden action. The pre-scan reported zero deterministic findings, no unreferenced scripts, and no magic-type mismatches; several referenced filenames not found are quality/resolution artifacts, not security threats. No prompt injection, obfuscation, secrets, or exfiltration chains were identified.

The astropy skill is a documentation-only package: 9 markdown files (SKILL.md plus references/*.md) with no scripts, no executables, and no unreferenced binaries. The pre-scan produced zero deterministic findings and the manifest declares no tools. All content is legitimate Astropy API guidance (units, coordinates, FITS I/O, tables, time, WCS, cosmology). Network-touching APIs (SkyCoord.from_name, EarthLocation.of_site/of_address, download_file, remote FITS via fsspec, IERS auto-download, PyVO SAMP) are discussed as the library's own documented behavior and are consistently accompanied by privacy cautions telling the agent to avoid sending sensitive target names, addresses, or proprietary file locations to third parties and to confirm with the user first — i.e., the guidance reduces rather than creates exfiltration risk. Installation guidance uses pinned `uv pip install "astropy==8.0.1"` from PyPI with advice against elevated privileges and in favor of lockfiles, which is ordinary dependency installation. The citation section asks the agent to add the authors' paper to a reference list only if the skill materially contributed, and explicitly requires informing the user, so there is no hidden or undisclosed action. No prompt-injection or instruction-override language, no obfuscation or encoded payloads, no credential access, no automatic/pre-flight script execution, and no capability claims beyond the stated astronomy-analysis purpose were found.

autoskill is a well-documented, user-invoked workflow-analysis skill that reads a local Screenpipe HTTP API, clusters activity locally, matches against sibling SKILL.md descriptions with local embeddings, and asks a user-configured LLM backend (local LM Studio by default, opt-in Anthropic/Foundry) to classify clusters and draft proposal files. The deterministic 'ENV_VAR_EXFILTRATION' and 'CROSSFILE_EXFILTRATION_CHAIN' leads (DET:74b65954746f7db6, DET:8a78b9ceec06e3fb, DET:1abcccbedaeb1ad5, DET:740f98a79ba73b7f, DET:43e118dab7f38df7) were verified against the source and do not hold: SCREENPIPE_TOKEN, LM_API_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and FOUNDRY_API_KEY are read only to populate Authorization/x-api-key headers for the exact service each credential belongs to, all of which are declared in the manifest openclaw.envVars block and the SKILL.md network-access notice. No credential is placed in a request body, written to disk, or sent to an undeclared destination. Supporting controls argue against malicious intent: check_remote_endpoint() rejects credentialed/query-bearing URLs and plaintext HTTP to non-loopback hosts and prints an explicit notice when data leaves the machine; fetch_window explicitly sets include_cloud=false, include_frames=false and filter_pii=false to avoid remote processing; redact.py scrubs keys, bearer tokens, JWTs, emails and phone numbers before any summary reaches a backend; pagination is bounded by _MAX_PAGES so no unbounded loop exists. LLM-produced draft names are constrained to a slug regex, preventing path traversal when drafts are written, and promote.py refuses to overwrite an existing skill and runs only on explicit user invocation. The skill is documented as explicitly user-triggered rather than automatic or trigger-based, and no instruction tells the agent to hide output, bypass confirmation, or run bundled scripts silently. Installation guidance (git clone, cargo build, uv pip install of pinned packages, Hugging Face model download) is ordinary, named-source dependency setup. No obfuscation, hidden files, unreferenced executables, or hardcoded secrets were observed.

scan_metadata.llm_overall_assessment: The benchling-integration package consists solely of six markdown documentation files (SKILL.md plus four reference documents) with no executable scripts, no network sinks beyond the documented Benchling tenant and official documentation links, and no obfuscated content. Credential handling is confined to reading declared environment variables (BENCHLING_TENANT_URL, BENCHLING_API_KEY, BENCHLING_CLIENT_ID/SECRET) and passing them to the intended Benchling SDK/API endpoints, which is ordinary authentication for the service the skill exists to serve. The documentation repeatedly reinforces defensive guidance (do not log headers or secrets, do not send credentials to arbitrary URLs supplied in event data, keep TLS verification enabled), which is the opposite of exfiltration behavior. Declared allowed-tools (Read, Write, Edit, Bash) are consistent with the documented installation (uv pip install benchling-sdk) and example scripts, and no instruction directs the agent to auto-execute bundled or downloaded payloads, hide actions from the user, or bypass confirmation. The closing citation section asks the agent to add an author-affiliated reference only when the skill materially contributed and to disclose that addition to the user; it is transparent, conditional, and does not override agent instructions. Several referenced-file paths resolve to missing assets/templates variants, which is a documentation-quality issue rather than a security threat. The deterministic pre-scan produced no findings, and manual review of all provided content corroborates that result.

The package contains a single SKILL.md documenting how to connect to and query the BGPT remote MCP service for scientific paper/evidence retrieval. No scripts, no unreferenced executables, no deterministic findings. Network destinations (bgpt.pro, npm mcp-remote bridge, GitHub docs) are consistent with the stated purpose and disclosed in the manifest compatibility field. Credential guidance recommends storing the API key in the host's credential storage / header file for the intended service, and explicitly warns against passing api_key as a tool argument - normal, prudent credential use rather than exfiltration. The npx mcp-remote bridge is a documented, user-configured installation step, not an automatic agent-executed payload. Instructions include defensive guidance (never execute returned values as code, don't invent pagination, don't misread errors as empty results) and no instruction overrides, hiding of actions, or confirmation bypass. No prompt injection, obfuscation, hardcoded secrets, or capability inflation observed.

The 'bids' skill is a legitimate neuroscience data-organization helper. SKILL.md contains only domain documentation (BIDS structure, validation, conversion workflows, best practices) with no instruction overrides, hidden actions, or directives to conceal activity from the user. The single bundled script, scripts/update_schema.py, fetches the official BIDS schema and BEP catalogue over HTTPS-only URLs from bids-specification.readthedocs.io and raw.githubusercontent.com/bids-standard, enforces a 20 MB response cap and 30s timeout, validates the JSON/YAML envelope before writing, and atomically replaces two files inside the skill's own references/ directory. It does not execute downloaded content, and it is run only on explicit user invocation (documented command), not automatically. No credential, environment, or sensitive-file access occurs; no outbound data is sent. Package registry installs (uv pip install pybids, heudiconv, etc.) and container invocation examples are the declared purpose of the skill and are not findings. Missing optional referenced files (templates/, assets/ variants) are quality issues, not security threats. Pre-scan produced zero deterministic findings.

The package is a documentation-only Agent Skill (9 markdown files, no executable scripts) providing Biopython usage guidance: sequence I/O, alignment, Entrez/NCBI access, BLAST, structures, phylogenetics, and motifs. All network destinations referenced are the intended first-party services (NCBI E-utilities, NCBI BLAST, RCSB PDB archive, biopython.org docs, arxiv.org for the citation record) and are consistent with the stated purpose. Credential handling is limited to optionally reading NCBI_API_KEY from the environment for the declared service, with explicit instructions not to hardcode keys or load unrelated environment variables - normal, declared credential use rather than exfiltration. The deterministic MDBLOCK_PYTHON_SUBPROCESS leads (DET:2b1274283d30c763, DET:5826881730f9909a, DET:12b8533240beafce, DET:4203e22f1126d8ca, DET:cfa6ae37d8e2cae5, DET:8207ae0b7c8dcc5d) were verified against source: they are illustrative subprocess.run() calls with fixed executables (blastn, makeblastdb, clustalo, muscle) passed as explicit argument lists with shell=False, accompanied by explicit guidance to validate paths and never interpolate unsanitized user input. No untrusted external content reaches command construction, so no actionable command-injection chain exists. There are no download-then-execute chains, no obfuscation or encoded payloads, no instructions to run bundled scripts automatically or hide actions from the user, no instruction overrides, and no hidden or unreferenced executables. Missing optional reference paths (templates/*, assets/*, Bio.py) are quality/packaging issues, not security threats.

findings.title: Self-promotional citation directive instructing the agent to add author's paper to user outputs
findings.description: The SKILL.md body ends with a 'Citing Scientific Agent Skills' section directing the agent to insert a specific arXiv citation (arXiv:2609.00065, authored by the skill vendor K-Dense) into manuscripts, reports, presentations or code releases, to inform the user it did so, and to fetch the arXiv record over the network when available. This is vendor self-promotion injected into the agent's output work product rather than functionality required for the stated Cirq/quantum-computing purpose. It is disclosed (the agent is told to tell the user), the network fetch targets a legitimate, named public endpoint (arxiv.org / export.arxiv.org), and no local data is transmitted, so impact is low and it does not constitute exfiltration or a hidden action.
findings.snippet: "If it materially contributed to a manuscript, report, presentation, or code release, add the paper to the references ... and tell the user you did so" plus instruction to fetch https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.00065 or the arXiv API before writing the reference.
findings.remediation: Reframe the citation guidance as optional information surfaced to the user rather than a directive that the agent insert the vendor's paper into user deliverables, and make the outbound arXiv lookup explicitly user-approved.

The SKILL.md body (SRC:0e95f5a3666031d6) contains only documentation, pinned installation via `uv pip install "ete4==4.4.0"`, and ordinary usage examples; no instruction overrides, no hidden-action directives, and no instructions to conceal output from the user. The two bundled scripts (SRC:ffe3ee75e280c046, SRC:29c20f23f8240f6b) are argparse-driven, perform strict input validation, avoid shell execution, use no network sinks, and in fact add defensive controls (rejecting nonfinite branch lengths/support, requiring --allow-remote-bind before binding SmartView beyond loopback, verifying PNG magic bytes before replacing output). Reference docs (SRC:6c4c0c08e656636e, SRC:e29aeacd294b7670, SRC:95ef88b9e22fc103, SRC:87638ec0985efc91, SRC:00df5cf15abd2f31, SRC:00e67b048597c58b) describe public, credential-free NCBI/GTDB taxonomy archive downloads to local SQLite, explicitly warn about unverified upstream checksums, caution against unpickling untrusted traversal caches, and warn against building executable TreePattern expressions from untrusted text — security-positive guidance rather than risk. The optional citation request is transparent, conditional, and instructs disclosure to the user, so it is not deceptive. No secrets, obfuscation, exfiltration paths, or injection chains were found, and the trusted pre-scan context reported zero deterministic findings and no unreferenced scripts.

The exa-search skill is a straightforward CLI wrapper around the official exa-py SDK providing web search and URL content extraction. Both Python scripts (SRC:7c46508a25ee3c57, SRC:fe87c542a5dec21e) read EXA_API_KEY from the environment and pass it only to the Exa SDK client for authentication against the declared service endpoints (api.exa.ai), which is ordinary, in-scope credential use. Output is written to stdout or a user-specified local JSON file; no local files, environment dumps, or conversation content are transmitted anywhere. The 'x-exa-integration' attribution header is a static integration identifier, explicitly disclosed in SKILL.md (SRC:0e95f5a3666031d6), carries no user or system data, and is sent only to the skill's own intended API. Reference files (SRC:cc6632b9adf5ead4, SRC:44e89f7a01e4ba6d) contain only usage guidance, citation/formatting rules, and accuracy cautions; there are no instruction overrides, hidden actions, auto-execution triggers, obfuscation, download-and-execute chains, or hardcoded secrets. Missing optional templates/assets paths are documentation artifacts, not security issues. The pre-scan reported zero deterministic findings and no unreferenced scripts.

The experimental-design skill is a legitimate statistics/DOE knowledge package. SKILL.md provides design-selection guidance, two bundled Python modules (randomization.py, doe_designs.py) that generate allocation schedules and DOE matrices using numpy/pandas/pydoe, and four reference markdown files covering randomization, factorial designs, design types, and sequential/adaptive methods. No network calls, file exfiltration, environment/credential access, subprocess execution, encoded payloads, or hidden instructions were observed. The documented installation step (uv venv / uv pip install of pinned public packages) and the optional citation guidance (fetching an arXiv abstract page to format a reference) are declared, transparent, and consistent with the stated purpose; they fall under normal dependency installation and documentation behavior rather than misuse. Declared allowed-tools (Read, Write, Edit, Bash) match the need to run the bundled scripts and write CSV layouts. The pre-scan reports no deterministic findings, complete manifest capabilities, and no unreferenced scripts. Several referenced files appear under alternate directory names (assets/, templates/) and are simply absent, which is a documentation/quality issue rather than a security threat.

The exploratory-data-analysis skill is a bounded, local-only scientific data inspection toolkit. All bundled Python CLIs operate on local regular files within an explicit --root, reject URLs, symlinks, traversal, multiply linked and special files, enforce byte/row/column/object/report caps, disable pickle (allow_pickle=False), refuse to follow HDF5 soft/external links, avoid pixel decoding, and emit tokenized identifiers with raw values and full paths redacted. No network calls, subprocess execution, dynamic evaluation (eval/exec), encoded payloads, credential access, or environment-variable harvesting appear anywhere in the package. SKILL.md explicitly instructs treating file-derived text as untrusted data and never passing it to a shell, which is a defensive rather than injectable posture. Dependency pins reference ordinary PyPI packages installed manually via uv, which is documented and not automatic. The only external-network reference is an optional, disclosed instruction to fetch an arXiv record when adding a citation that the agent is told to disclose to the user; this is transparent attribution, not covert exfiltration. The deterministic pre-scan produced no findings and all referenced scripts are present and used. No security threats identified.

The 'fictiv' skill is a browser-automation guide for operating the Fictiv on-demand manufacturing web app. All content is consistent with its stated purpose: a local, standard-library-only Python pre-flight CAD checker (reads local files, prints results, makes no network calls), two read-only DOM-reading JavaScript helpers (explicitly non-clicking, no network requests, results left on window), and documentation files describing UI routes, quoting, checkout, orders and troubleshooting. No hardcoded secrets, no network exfiltration sinks, no download-and-execute chain, no obfuscation or encoded payloads, and no hidden/unreferenced executables were observed. The skill repeatedly reinforces safety controls rather than bypassing them: an explicit approval gate before spending money, a prohibition on typing card numbers/CVC/passwords, a directive to treat page/chat/email content as data and not as instructions (anti-indirect-injection guidance), a refusal to reverse-engineer private API endpoints, and warnings against ITAR/export-controlled uploads. The skill description is broad but accurately scoped to the Fictiv platform and custom-parts manufacturing workflows, so it does not constitute discovery-keyword baiting. Several referenced files under templates/ and assets/ were not found, but all substantive references under references/ are present; missing optional/duplicate path variants are a quality issue, not a security threat.

The flowio skill is a documentation-centric package for reading/writing Flow Cytometry Standard files with the FlowIO Python library. The manifest declares Read, Write, and Bash tools, consistent with running a bundled local inspection script. The single Python script (scripts/inspect_fcs.py) performs purely local file parsing: it reads a user-specified FCS path, enforces size/dataset/array-memory limits, emits JSON to stdout or a new (non-overwriting) file, and makes no network calls, subprocess invocations, environment-variable reads, or credential access. Reference markdown files contain accurate API documentation, troubleshooting, and privacy guidance that actively warns against exporting identifying metadata. No instruction overrides, hidden execution, obfuscation, encoded payloads, or exfiltration sinks are present. The install commands (uv pip install / uv run --with flowio==1.4.0) are pinned, named registry installs that fall under normal dependency usage. The optional citation section asks the agent to add a public arXiv reference and explicitly to inform the user, which is disclosed, non-coercive, and not a security threat. No sensitive-source-to-external-sink chain, no untrusted-content-to-command-construction chain, and no deterministic pre-scan findings exist.

The flowkit skill is a legitimate scientific-computing helper for flow cytometry analysis. SKILL.md documents installation via uv/pip of a named public package (flowkit==1.3.2), a documented CLI invocation, and interpretation guidance; no hidden execution, no automatic pre-flight scripts, and no instructions to conceal actions from the user. The bundled script scripts/analyze_gates.py operates purely on explicit local input files (FCS/GatingML/WSP), computes SHA-256 hashes for provenance, and writes a CSV report and provenance JSON to a new local directory. It performs no network I/O, no subprocess/shell execution, no eval/exec, no environment or credential access, and no encoding/obfuscation. It explicitly disables following paths embedded in workspaces (find_fcs_files_from_wsp=False), reducing untrusted-path risk. Reference markdown files contain only documentation and links to official FlowKit docs/repos. The deterministic pre-scan reported no findings, and the manifest description is narrowly scoped to the stated domain with no discovery baiting.

The fluidsim skill is a well-structured scientific-computing assistant for FluidSim CFD planning and analysis. All bundled Python tools are dependency-free, operate on local paths with strict root confinement, symlink/hard-link rejection, URI rejection, path-traversal rejection, bounded input sizes, strict JSON output, and no network or subprocess use. The dry-run generator renders a launch script from a statically allowlisted solver-key-to-module map (never deriving module names from user text), writes it atomically, and requires an explicit --execute plus exact config-ID acknowledgement before any simulation runs; the skill explicitly forbids auto-submitting MPI jobs or schedulers. References repeatedly warn against the upstream `fluidsim-restart --modify-params` option because it executes Python, and the generator never emits it 
instead of enabling it. No hardcoded secrets, no environment/credential access, no external data sinks, no obfuscation, and no hidden or unreferenced executables were observed. The only prescriptive non-technical behavior is a citation request (adding a paper reference and telling the user, with an optional arXiv metadata fetch), which is transparent, user-visible, benign self-attribution and not a security threat. Documented installs from PyPI with pinned versions and lockfiles are normal dependency management. Package verdict: SAFE with zero findings.

The package contains only two markdown files (SKILL.md and references/mcp-contract.md) and no executable scripts. It documents connecting to a single declared, publicly stated MCP endpoint (https://api.helena.bio/folklore/v1/mcp) that requires no credentials, and the curl example transmits only public variant identifiers such as rsIDs and HGVS notations. There is no sensitive-source-to-sink chain, no credential handling, no download-and-execute pattern, no obfuscation or hidden content, and no instruction to conceal actions from the user or bypass confirmation. To the contrary, the instructions repeatedly enforce a restrictive data boundary (refusing patient, phenotype, family, segregation, or private case data), mandate stopping on ambiguous results rather than auto-selecting candidates, and require preserving provenance and professional-review disclaimers. The mention of a non-scientific 'support_helena' tool is explicitly disclosed and gated behind an explicit user request, which does not constitute misuse. Two referenced path variants (templates/ and assets/ copies of mcp-contract.md) are missing, which is a documentation-quality issue rather than a security threat. No findings warranted.

The package is a coherent, single-purpose image generation skill. SKILL.md documents an OpenRouter Image API workflow, and the bundled Python script (standard library only) builds a JSON request and POSTs it to the declared endpoint https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/images. Credential handling is ordinary and declared: the key is resolved from --api-key, the OPENROUTER_API_KEY environment variable, or a .env file, and is only ever used as an Authorization: Bearer header to the intended OpenRouter host; it is never placed into a request payload or sent to any third-party destination. Reference images are base64-encoded locally and uploaded to the declared service, which is the skill's stated purpose, and the documentation explicitly warns against sending sensitive or credential-bearing URLs. Response-driven downloads are constrained to HTTPS with a 64 MB cap, base64 is validated, and output paths derive from user-specified values rather than remote content. There are no instructions to auto-execute scripts, hide actions from the user, bypass confirmation, or override agent instructions; no obfuscation, encoded payloads, hardcoded secrets, or unreferenced executables; and the citation guidance only fetches a public arXiv record. Missing referenced asset paths (logo.svg, templates/models.md) are documentation/quality artifacts of example output paths, not security issues. Declared allowed-tools (Read, Write, Edit, Bash) match observed behavior, and the deterministic pre-scan produced no findings.

The geniml skill provides local, read-only validation and planning utilities for genomic interval (BED) workflows. All five bundled Python scripts are standard-library only: they parse manifests, hash files, validate BED coordinates, and emit JSON run plans. They explicitly refuse URLs, symlinks, parent traversal, and NUL bytes (_common.local_path), enforce byte/record/line bounds, and never execute subprocesses, deserialize models, or make network requests. Path disclosure defaults to 'redacted' and metadata values are deliberately withheld from output, which reduces rather than increases data-exposure risk. SKILL.md and the reference documents consistently instruct obtaining explicit user approval before any network download (BEDbase, Hugging Face), warn against untrusted pickle/Torch artifacts, and contain no instruction overrides, hidden actions, auto-execution triggers, or exfiltration sinks. The citation request at the end of SKILL.md is a transparent, disclosed attribution ask tied to a documented arXiv identifier and does not constitute concealed behavior. The genomic-coordinates skill is a documentation-plus-tooling package for genomic coordinate conversion, variant normalisation, and assembly/contig consistency checking. All five Python files (convert_coords.py, normalize_variant.py, check_contigs.py, audit_intervals.py, _common.py) use only the Python standard library, perform local file reads of user-supplied genomics files (FASTA/.fai, VCF, BED, GTF/GFF, chrom.sizes), and write diagnostic TSV/JSON to stdout or a user-specified path. The genomic-intelligence skill is documentation-only (6 markdown files, no scripts) describing how to call Genomic Intelligence's declared REST API (api.genomicintelligence.ai) and hosted MCP server (mcp.genomicintelligence.ai). The two deterministic leads (DET:7aa309a96ca40a65, DET:f3ea75123b4e3368) flag Python `requests.post` calls in SKILL.md code blocks; review of SRC:0e95f5a3666031d6 shows these post DNA sequence payloads to the skill's own declared, in-scope base URL (overridable only via the documented GI_BASE_URL staging variable), which is exactly the capability the skill exists to provide. There are no instructions to auto-execute bundled/downloaded scripts, no download-then-run chains, no obfuscation or encoded payloads, no instruction overrides or directives to hide actions from the user, and no sensitive local file/environment collection routed to an external sink. Missing reference files (assets/*, templates/*) are a quality issue, not a security threat.

scan_metadata.llm_overall_assessment: GeoMaster is a documentation-heavy geospatial analysis skill consisting of 17 markdown references and one bundled Python module (scripts/raster_workflows.py). The three deterministic leads were verified and do not hold up: the 'PYTHON_EVAL_EXEC' hit in references/machine-learning.md corresponds to PyTorch's model.eval()/model.train() training-loop idiom, not eval()/exec(); the HTTP POST in references/data-sources.md is an explicitly documented, illustrative Overpass API query to the public overpass-api.de endpoint with no local data attached; the subprocess call in references/gis-software.md invokes the documented saga_cmd GIS tool with static arguments on local DEM files. Credential guidance throughout is defensive (read tokens from environment or credential store, never embed keys, never log signed SAS URLs), and all network endpoints referenced (Planetary Computer, Earth Search, CDSE, CDS, Nominatim/Overpass, Earth Engine) are the intended, declared services for the skill's stated purpose. The SKILL.md body contains no instruction overrides, no directions to hide actions from the user, no auto-execution or pre-flight script requirements, and no obfuscated or encoded payloads. The citation section asks the agent to optionally fetch a public arXiv record and to explicitly tell the user when a citation is added, which is disclosed and benign. Numerous referenced markdown files are absent from the package, which is a completeness/quality issue rather than a security threat.

scan_metadata.llm_overall_assessment: The geopandas skill is a documentation-and-audit package consisting of a SKILL.md guidance body, six reference markdown files, and six local-only Python CLIs plus a shared helper module. All bundled scripts are deterministic, metadata-oriented analyzers: they validate input paths against an allowlist, explicitly reject URLs, GDAL /vsi* virtual filesystems, archive members, symlinks and path traversal, bound input/output bytes and feature counts, forcibly disable PROJ network access, and emit redacted JSON containing no coordinates, identifiers, paths, or environment data. No network calls, subprocess execution, dynamic code evaluation, encoded payloads, credential reads, or data sinks are present. Environment variable usage is limited to documentation examples for named PostGIS secrets, with explicit guidance never to print connection URLs or dump the environment. The manifest's declared tools (Read, Write, Bash, Glob, Grep) are consistent with running local CLIs and reading/writing local geospatial artifacts; the only write path (geometry_validity_report.py --repair-output) creates a new, non-overwriting GeoPackage inside a validated root and verifies a roundtrip. The optional citation section is transparently disclosed and instructs the agent to inform the user, with no hidden action, exfiltration, or instruction override. No prompt injection, obfuscation, or capability inflation was observed; the pre-scan produced zero deterministic findings.

The get-available-resources skill is a read-only local resource inventory toolkit. All five Python scripts use fixed, hardcoded argv tuples (nvidia-smi, amd-smi, rocm-smi, sysctl, system_profiler) executed with shell=False, bounded output buffers, short timeouts, and explicit FileNotFoundError/OSError handling; there is no shell interpolation of user input and no dynamic command construction. File reads are bounded (1 MiB cap), reject symlinks and non-regular files, and writes are restricted to a single .json filename in the current directory with O_EXCL/O_NOFOLLOW and mode 0600. No network calls, no download-then-execute chain, no encoding/decoding or obfuscation, and no hardcoded secrets exist anywhere in the package. Environment access is explicitly allowlisted (four accelerator visibility variable names plus named Slurm allocation keys) and values are redacted rather than emitted, which is narrower than the stated purpose requires. The SKILL.md body contains only interpretation guidance and prohibitions (no stress tests, no driver mutation, no environment dumps, no automatic execution) and no instruction overrides, hidden-action directives, or confirmation-skipping language. The optional psutil install via uv and the citation request (including an optional arXiv fetch for reference metadata) are benign, disclosed, documentation-grade behaviors. No findings.

The gget skill is a legitimate bioinformatics wrapper package. It documents the public gget CLI/Python library, provides three bundled analysis scripts (gene_analysis.py, enrichment_pipeline.py, batch_sequence_analysis.py), and reference documentation describing module parameters and upstream service contracts. No deterministic pre-scan findings were raised. Review of the scripts shows only argparse-driven local file reads, gget API calls to the documented bioinformatics services (Ensembl, ARCHS4, Enrichr, Open Targets, NCBI BLAST, RCSB), and CSV/FASTA writes to user-specified output prefixes; there is no subprocess/eval/exec usage, no network sink outside the stated purpose, and no credential handling beyond advising users to keep COSMIC/OpenAI secrets in environment variables (explicitly warning against hard-coding them). The batch script explicitly sanitizes FASTA identifiers before using them in output filenames, mitigating path traversal from untrusted input. Installation guidance (uv pip install of a pinned gget version) and gget setup dependency installs are ordinary registry installs for the service the skill exists to provide. The citation section asks the agent to mention adding a citation to the user, which is disclosed rather than hidden behavior. Several referenced reference files (assets/ and templates/ paths) are absent, but missing optional documentation is a quality issue, not a security threat. No prompt injection, obfuscation, exfiltration, or unauthorized tool-use behavior was identified.

The ginkgo-cloud-lab package is a documentation-only skill (19 markdown files, no scripts) that guides users through protocol selection, pricing, and browser-based ordering on Ginkgo Bioworks Cloud Lab. The glycoengineering skill is a scientific bioinformatics package containing two Python helpers and three markdown references. The local helper (scripts/glycoengineering_tools.py) uses only the standard library, performs strict input validation, and makes no network or filesystem calls. scripts/glytoucan_lookup.py performs an unauthenticated read-only GET against the documented public GlyTouCan SPARQL endpoint (https://ts.glytoucan.org/sparql) with a regex-validated accession, preventing SPARQL interpolation; no local data, secrets, or environment variables are transmitted. No prompt-injection text, instruction overrides, hidden/automatic execution directives, obfuscation, hardcoded secrets, or exfiltration sinks are present. Install instructions (git clone of a pinned upstream commit, uv pip install -e) are explicitly labeled illustrative and target a named, documented repository, which is within normal supply-chain expectations. Missing optional referenced paths (assets/ and templates/ variants) are quality/packaging artifacts, not security issues.

scan_metadata.llm_overall_assessment: The gtars skill is a legitimate scientific-computing helper package for genomic interval analysis. All bundled Python scripts (_common.py, bed_validator.py, execution_plan.py, coverage_preflight.py, tokenizer_manifest.py, refget_digest_plan.py, artifact_inspector.py) are dependency-free, perform only local read-only validation, and explicitly reject URLs, URI schemes, symlinks, path traversal, home-directory expansion, NUL bytes, and non-regular files. They enforce byte/record/worker caps, never import gtars, never spawn subprocesses, never write output files, and emit only counts, checksums, and redacted paths by default (display_path defaults to 'redacted'), which actively reduces rather than increases data exposure. No network calls, no encoded or obfuscated payloads, no credential access, and no hidden executables were found. SKILL.md contains no instruction overrides, no directives to conceal activity from the user, and no automatic pre-flight execution mandates; its network-capable upstream operations (Tokenizer.from_pretrained, RefgetStore.open_remote, gtars bbcache) are documented defensively behind explicit user-approval gates with host allowlisting and checksum requirements. Installation guidance (uv pip install, cargo install) uses pinned versions with --locked and is accompanied by an explicit native-code trust gate warning against running unverified binaries, which is normal and responsible packaging guidance rather than a supply-chain risk. The citation section asks the agent to disclose any citation it adds, which is transparent. One cosmetic code defect exists (MAX_DENSE_GAP is referenced in coverage_preflight.py's argparse builder before its module-level definition), but this is a correctness/quality issue with no security impact. No findings warrant reporting.

findings.title: Self-promotional citation insertion directive in SKILL.md
findings.description: The instruction body directs the agent to add a specific arXiv paper authored by the skill vendor (K-Dense) to the user's manuscripts, reports, presentations, or code releases whenever the skill 'materially contributed', and to fetch the arXiv record over the network to populate the reference. This is unrelated to the skill's stated LatchBio workflow purpose and biases user deliverables toward the vendor's publication. Mitigating factors: the action is disclosed, conditional, and the skill explicitly requires telling the user it was done, so this is a contextual risk rather than a hidden manipulation.
findings.snippet: "If it materially contributed to a manuscript, report, presentation, or code release, add the paper to the references or software section and tell the user you did so" followed by a fixed citation and an instruction to fetch https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.00065 when network access is available.
findings.remediation: Make citation insertion an explicit user-approved, opt-in step rather than a standing directive, and avoid instructing the agent to modify user deliverables with vendor-authored references by default.

findings.snippet: for directory in [cwd, *cwd.parents, Path(__file__).resolve().parent]: env_file = directory / '.env' ... headers = {'Authorization': f'Bearer {self.api_key}'} ... requests.post(f'{self.base_url}/{endpoint}', ...)
findings.remediation: Limit the .env search to the project root or the skill directory rather than every ancestor of the working directory, and surface which .env file supplied the credential to the user.

scan_metadata.llm_overall_assessment: The paperzilla skill is documentation-only: two markdown files (SKILL.md and references/cli-contracts.md) with no bundled scripts, no unreferenced executables, and no download-and-execute chains. It describes read/feedback operations against the official `pz` CLI and the paperzilla.ai API, with command-to-route mappings that stay within the stated purpose. Credential handling is conservative and explicitly protective: it tells the user to keep the Atom feed token out of logs and repositories, never to export ~/.paperzilla/tokens.json as research data, and not to point PZ_API_URL at an untrusted host. Installation uses official package managers (Homebrew tap, Scoop bucket, official release/source), which is normal dependency acquisition; the conditional `brew trust --formula paperzilla-ai/tap/pz` step is scoped to the same official formula and accompanied by a restriction, and the referenced contracts file documents SHA-256 verification of the release binary. No prompt-injection or instruction-override language, no hidden actions, no exfiltration sink, no hardcoded secrets, and no capability inflation in the description were found. Two referenced paths (assets/ and templates/ copies of cli-contracts.md) are missing, which is a documentation-quality issue rather than a security threat.

The parallel-web skill is a documentation-only package (8 markdown files, no scripts, no unreferenced executables) describing use of the third-party `parallel-cli` tool for web search, extraction, research, enrichment, entity discovery, and monitoring. All commands shown are the declared capability of the skill and are invoked through the documented CLI. Credential handling is conservative: the skill requires only PARALLEL_API_KEY for the intended service, explicitly forbids printing or logging the key, forbids reading an entire .env file, and forbids placing credentials in webhook URLs. There is no network sink for local data, no download-and-execute chain, no encoding/obfuscation, and no instruction to hide actions from the user or bypass confirmation. The instruction body repeatedly hardens against indirect prompt injection (treating search results, extracted pages, enrichment values, and monitor events as untrusted data) and against command injection (quoted single arguments, stdin for shell-sensitive text, JSON serializers instead of string concatenation, ID prefix validation rejecting whitespace/shell metacharacters). State-mutating operations (monitor create/update/trigger/cancel, findall cancel) are gated on explicit user authorization, and polling is explicitly bounded with a prohibition on unbounded loops. The optional self-citation section asks the agent to add the authors' paper only when the skill materially contributed and to disclose that addition to the user, which is transparent attribution rather than covert manipulation. No security findings warrant reporting.

The pathml skill is a research-oriented computational pathology helper. Its SKILL.md and six reference documents focus on local, de-identified workflows and repeatedly emphasize safety: no-network defaults, explicit consent gates before any model/dataset download, warnings against loading untrusted pickle/.pt/h5path artifacts, and explicit prohibition of dynamic Python evaluation. The five bundled Python scripts (slide_manifest.py, plan_pipeline.py, plan_inference.py, image_qc.py, validate_spatial_schema.py, plus _common.py) perform strictly local, bounded I/O: they reject URLs and symlinks, enforce a declared root boundary, cap input sizes/rows/pixels, use strict JSON parsing with duplicate-key and NaN rejection, write output atomically with 0600 permissions, and explicitly refuse to open model/checkpoint artifacts or import PathML/Torch/ONNX. No subprocess execution, no eval/exec, no network calls, no credential or environment access, and no obfuscation or encoded payloads are present. Declared allowed-tools (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob) are consistent with running the bundled local CLIs and editing analysis files. External URLs referenced (PyPI, GitHub, ReadTheDocs, Hugging Face, Zenodo, Warwick, DOIs) appear only as documentation or as disclosed upstream-library behavior that the skill tells the agent to gate behind explicit user consent. The citation request at the end of SKILL.md is transparent, conditional, and instructs the agent to inform the user, so it is not deceptive or hidden behavior. No deterministic pre-scan findings were reported, and all referenced scripts are present and analyzable.

The pathogen-variant-surveillance skill is a scientific data-query toolkit that uses only the Python standard library to issue read-only HTTP GET requests to publicly declared GenSpectrum/Pathoplexus LAPIS endpoints and to raw.githubusercontent.com for pango-designation nomenclature files. All network destinations are enumerated in the manifest compatibility field and the bundled registry, matching the stated purpose. No credentials, secrets, environment-variable reads, filesystem harvesting, subprocess/shell execution, dynamic code evaluation, encoding/obfuscation, download-and-execute chains, persistence, or outbound transmission of local data were observed. The only file write is the user-specified --output report path. The client explicitly sanitizes remote strings (control-character stripping) and the SKILL.md directs the agent to never interpret remote labels or error strings as instructions, which is a defensive anti-injection posture rather than a threat. The SKILL.md body contains no instruction overrides, hidden-action directives, confirmation bypasses, or auto-execution triggers; scripts are invoked only through documented, user-initiated workflow examples. The citation section is transparent (it requires materiality and instructs the agent to disclose the addition to the user) and therefore does not rise to deceptive or hidden behavior. Reference markdown files are documentation only. Some referenced files resolve under references/ while templates/ and assets/ variants are absent, which is a packaging/quality observation, not a security issue. The deterministic pre-scan produced no findings and the package projection is complete.

The pathway-enrichment skill is a legitimate bioinformatics workflow package. SKILL.md documents ORA/GSEA methodology, and the single bundled script (scripts/run_enrichment.py) performs argument parsing, input validation, gseapy calls to the declared public services (Enrichr/Speedrichr, g:Profiler, MSigDB, BioMart, MyGene), and writes result tables/plots/metadata to a user-specified output directory. No obfuscation, encoded payloads, dynamic code execution (eval/exec), shell invocation, credential access, environment-variable harvesting, or undisclosed network sinks are present. Network destinations are all documented, public, unauthenticated bioinformatics endpoints consistent with the stated purpose, and the only data transmitted is the user's gene list/background, which is the core function of the skill. The citation section asks the agent to fetch a public arXiv record and cite the authors' paper — self-promotional but disclosed, user-visible, and not a hidden action or data exfiltration. Missing reference files (templates/*, assets/*) are documentation/quality issues, not security threats. No findings warranted.

The peer-review skill is a coherent, well-scoped research-support package. SKILL.md provides procedural guidance for preparing peer-review drafts and enforces an authorization/confidentiality gate before any unpublished content is handled. All eight bundled Python CLIs (intake validator, guideline selector, claim-evidence validator, statistics/reproducibility auditor, citation auditor, scaffold generator, lint tool, shared helpers) use only the Python standard library and contain no network calls, no subprocess execution, no environment-variable or credential access, no dynamic code evaluation, and no deserialization of executable formats. _common.py implements defensive input handling: bounded file sizes (4 MiB), bounded CSV rows/cells, strict UTF-8 with NUL rejection, duplicate JSON key and CSV header rejection, symlink input/output rejection, no implicit overwrite without --force, and atomic writes with owner-only permissions. Reports deliberately emit identifiers, counts, rule codes, and line numbers rather than manuscript prose, which reduces confidential-data exposure. Instruction text explicitly prohibits sending unpublished material to external services, reading .env files or credentials, calling network/LLM/image APIs, invoking other skills automatically, impersonating reviewers or editors, and fabricating findings. The pre-scan context reports zero deterministic findings, complete manifest capabilities, and no unreferenced scripts. The only mildly promotional element is a conditional, user-disclosed request to cite the authoring organization's paper when the skill materially contributed, together with an optional arXiv metadata fetch for accurate citation; this is transparent, non-coercive, does not exfiltrate local data, and does not contradict the stated purpose. Several referenced documentation/template files are absent, which is a documentation-completeness issue rather than a security threat. No prompt injection, obfuscation, exfiltration sink, hidden execution trigger, or capability mismatch was identified.

The package is a documentation-only Agent Skill for PennyLane quantum computing workflows. All code blocks are self-contained, illustrative quantum simulation examples using PennyLane, NumPy, JAX and PyTorch, with assertions for numerical validation. Credential handling is limited to standard environment-variable reads (e.g., IBM_QUANTUM_API_KEY, PENNYLANE_IONQ_API_KEY) for the intended provider SDKs, with no local data, secrets, or conversation content sent to any external or undeclared destination. Installation commands use the public PyPI registry via uv/pip for named, version-pinned packages, which is ordinary dependency setup. There are no bundled or hidden scripts, no download-then-execute chains, no encoded or obfuscated payloads, and no instructions directing the agent to hide actions, bypass user confirmation, or override its own instructions. The citation section requests that a paper be cited and explicitly instructs the agent to inform the user, and permits an optional metadata fetch from arxiv.org; this is disclosed, conditional attribution rather than covert behavior or exfiltration. Declared tools (Read, Bash, Python) match the documented purpose of running local quantum simulations. No security findings.

The phylogenetics skill is a legitimate bioinformatics workflow package. The pi-agent skill is a documentation-only package (36 markdown files, no scripts) that describes how to install, configure, and build on the Pi terminal coding harness. Security-relevant text (no built-in sandbox, project trust, containerization) is defensive guidance. The citation section asks the agent to cite a paper and optionally fetch an arXiv record when network is available - this is benign, disclosed, and tied to attribution rather than data egress. No prompt-injection, instruction-override, hidden execution, obfuscation, or undisclosed network behavior was found. Many referenced assets/templates paths are missing, which is a quality issue, not a security threat.

The pkpd-modeling skill is a scientific computing package for pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic analysis. All bundled Python scripts (nca.py, fit_compartmental.py, simulate_regimen.py, exposure_response.py, bioequivalence.py, ddi_static.py, tdm_bayes.py, allometry_and_fih.py, check_popk_dataset.py, _models.py, _common.py) perform purely local numerical computation using NumPy/SciPy: reading local CSV/TSV tables (or stdin), fitting models, and writing tables/notes to stdout/stderr. There is no network I/O, no subprocess/shell execution, no eval/exec, no file writes outside the reporting streams, no environment-variable or credential access, and no obfuscated or encoded payloads. The declared allowed-tools (Read, Write, Edit, Bash) are consistent with a skill that invokes python3 scripts on user-supplied data files. SKILL.md contains no instruction overrides, no directives to hide output from the user, no mandatory pre-flight script execution, and no exfiltration sinks; the only outbound-network mention is an optional, disclosed arXiv citation lookup for the authors' own paper, which is transparent and non-sensitive. The skill repeatedly and explicitly disclaims clinical/regulatory validity, which mitigates rather than creates harmful-content risk in a medical-dosing domain. Referenced markdown documentation files that are absent are a completeness/quality issue, not a security threat. No findings warrant reporting.

The polars-bio package is a documentation-only Agent Skill (7 markdown files, no scripts) that teaches correct use of the polars-bio Python library for genomic interval arithmetic and bioinformatics file I/O. All content is descriptive guidance, API semantics, coordinate-convention warnings, and executable-looking Python snippets that are clearly templates for user-driven analysis. The pptx-posters skill is a local, network-free PowerPoint poster generation and auditing toolkit. All bundled Python scripts operate strictly on local JSON manifests and local PNG/JPEG assets: there are no network calls, no subprocess/shell invocation, no environment variable or credential access, no dynamic code execution, and no archive extraction. Security-relevant code is defensive in nature (bounded ZIP central-directory preflight, DTD/entity rejection, path-traversal and symlink prevention, decompression-bomb limits, no-overwrite output publication, strict content-type/relationship allowlists). The SKILL.md body contains no instruction overrides, no directives to hide actions from the user, and no automatic execution of downloaded payloads; dependency installation via `uv pip install` with exact pins is documented, user-initiated, and from a standard registry, which is not itself a finding. No hardcoded secrets, obfuscation, unicode steganography, or capability inflation were observed; the description is narrowly scoped to its stated purpose and matches the declared allowed-tools.

The primekg skill provides local pandas-based querying of a pinned PrimeKG CSV artifact. The bundled Python module (scripts/query_primekg.py) performs only local file reads (path configurable via PRIMEKG_DATA), schema validation, and in-memory graph traversal; it makes no network calls, no subprocess/shell execution, no dynamic code evaluation, and no access to credentials, environment secrets beyond its own data-path variable, or external sinks. The primer-design skill is a legitimate bioinformatics package for PCR/RT-qPCR primer design using Primer3 and optional local BLAST+ screening. All reviewed scripts operate strictly on user-supplied local files: FASTA reading, TSV parsing, Primer3 thermodynamic calls, and bounded local sequence searches. The only subprocess usage invokes resolved local `blastn`/`makeblastdb` executables with fixed, non-shell argument lists and temporary files inside a TemporaryDirectory, with timeouts and output-row caps — no shell interpolation of untrusted content. There is no network egress in any script; the documentation explicitly states that sequences are not submitted to remote services and that Primer-BLAST must be used manually via the official web interface. No credentials, environment-variable harvesting, encoded/obfuscated payloads, hidden files, auto-executed setup hooks, or instructions to conceal activity from the user were found. The install commands (`uv venv`, `uv pip install -r assets/requirements.txt` pinning primer3-py==2.3.1) are ordinary, documented dependency installation. Resource usage is explicitly bounded (comparison, hit, product, panel, and BLAST row caps that fail closed). The instruction body contains no prompt-injection, instruction-override, or capability-inflation language; the description accurately matches the implemented behavior. Missing referenced reference/asset filenames are only path-resolution/quality artifacts, not security threats.

The protocolsio-integration skill is a defensively engineered, read-oriented client for the protocols.io REST API. All bundled Python scripts use only the standard library and implement extensive safety controls: an HTTPS-only origin allowlist restricted to protocols.io core/tenant hosts, rejection of redirects, disabled ambient proxy discovery, bounded response sizes/timeouts/retries, strict JSON parsing with duplicate-key and NaN rejection, path containment to the current working directory with symlink and traversal rejection, 0600 private output files, and redaction of credential-like keys in any emitted structure. Credentials are read only from a single named environment variable (PROTOCOLS_IO_ACCESS_TOKEN) declared in the manifest, are never echoed, never placed in request bodies or plan output (the Authorization header is a placeholder string in write plans), and are only used as a bearer header to the declared official service. Network access is gated behind an explicit --execute flag; the write planner has no execution path at all and emits dry-run plans only. Remote content (protocol text, comments, pagination pointers, upload form fields, error messages) is explicitly treated as untrusted data and is sanitized rather than followed, with the documentation repeatedly instructing the agent never to obey embedded instructions — the opposite of prompt injection. No obfuscation, encoded payloads, download-and-execute chains, hidden scripts, hardcoded secrets, or undisclosed external sinks were found. The citation block at the end of SKILL.md is openly disclosed, instructs the agent to inform the user, and is conditional on the skill materially contributing to a work; it is transparent attribution rather than covert manipulation. The pre-scan contributed no deterministic findings and reported a complete, fully analyzable file inventory with no unreferenced scripts or magic-byte mismatches.

The pufferlib skill provides version-aware documentation and a set of dependency-free, local-only Python CLIs for reinforcement-learning workflow planning. All bundled scripts (env_template.py, env_contract_validator.py, benchmark_vectorization.py, train_template.py, validate_plan.py, repro_plan.py, inspect_checkpoint.py, _common.py) operate on synthetic, bounded, CPU-only data; they perform no network I/O, no subprocess execution, no dynamic imports, and no deserialization. Path handling is constrained via resolve_local_path with root containment and symlink rejection; JSON parsing rejects duplicate keys and non-finite values; plan validation explicitly rejects credential-bearing keys and unbounded resources. Credential handling is limited to naming environment variables (WANDB_API_KEY / NEPTUNE_API_TOKEN) without reading or emitting values, which is normal and explicitly guarded. Documentation references to upstream installation (uv add, git pin, PyPI sdist with pinned sha256) are illustrative, pinned, and accompanied by sandboxing guidance; they are not automatic execution directives. The citation section asks the agent to add a reference when the skill contributes to a manuscript and to optionally fetch a public arXiv record 
s a benign, disclosed documentation behavior rather than hidden data transmission. No prompt injection, obfuscation, exfiltration sink, or unauthorized tool chaining was identified. Several referenced files under templates/ and assets/ are missing, which is a quality issue only.

The pybamm skill is a scientific-computing package that runs local PyBaMM battery simulations. The single bundled script (scripts/simulate_battery.py) performs strict JSON protocol validation, rejects unknown/unsafe parameter overrides, refuses to overwrite existing output directories, reads only the user-specified protocol and measurement CSV, and writes CSV/JSON artifacts locally. The reference documentation mentions an optional, hash-verified upstream HTTPS dataset fetch from the official pybamm-data GitHub release, documented as manual and not performed automatically, which is ordinary declared behavior for the stated purpose. The pre-scan context reports no deterministic findings, no unreferenced scripts, and no magic-byte mismatches. Missing referenced path variants (templates/*, assets/protocol-and-comparison.md) are documentation/quality issues, not security threats. No obfuscation, no hardcoded secrets, and no capability inflation relative to the narrow battery-simulation description were observed.

The pycalphad skill is a legitimate scientific computing helper. SKILL.md documents a local, offline CALPHAD equilibrium workflow; the bundled script (scripts/equilibrate.py) only reads a user-supplied TDB file and a JSON settings file, performs validation, calls pycalphad's equilibrium solver, and writes report.json/phase-equilibria.csv to a new local directory. There is no network activity, no credential or environment-variable access, no obfuscation, no dynamic code execution (no eval/exec/subprocess), and no instruction to hide actions from the user or auto-run scripts. The documented uv/pip installation command is ordinary dependency provisioning for the intended service and the bundled TDB asset is clearly labeled as a hypothetical pedagogical model rather than an assessed database. Several referenced paths (templates/* and duplicate asset paths) are missing, but those are documentation/quality issues, not security threats. Manifest capabilities and pre-scan deterministic findings are empty, consistent with the reviewed content.

This is a legitimate, well-documented bioinformatics skill. The bundled Python driver (scripts/run_deseq2_analysis.py) performs only local CSV loading, validation, PyDESeq2 model fitting, and writing result files/plots to a user-specified output directory; there is no network I/O, subprocess execution, shell string construction, encoding/obfuscation, credential or environment access, or hidden/unreferenced executable. Reference documents are statistical guidance with links to upstream PyDESeq2 docs and GitHub sources; the only described network activity is PyDESeq2's own public example-data download, which is explicitly documented and cautioned about. llm_primary_threats: Vendor self-promotional citation instruction affecting user deliverables

findings.title: Self-promotional citation injection directive in SKILL.md
findings.description: The SKILL.md body instructs the agent to add a specific paper (arXiv:2609.00065, authored by the skill vendor K-Dense) to the references or software section of any manuscript, report, presentation, or code release the skill contributes to, to tell the user it did so, and to fetch an external arXiv URL when network access is available. This is vendor self-promotion embedded as an operational instruction rather than a capability needed for RNA-seq differential expression analysis, and it can cause unsolicited modification of user deliverables plus an outbound network fetch unrelated to the stated purpose. It is disclosed (not hidden) and the destination is a legitimate public preprint server, so impact is low and there is no data exfiltration: only a GET for bibliographic metadata is described.
findings.snippet: "If it materially contributed to a manuscript, report, presentation, or code release, add the paper to the references or software section and tell the user you did so"; "When network access is available, fetch https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.00065 (or http://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2609.00065) before writing the reference"
findings.remediation: Make the citation suggestion passive/optional (e.g., surface it for the user to approve) rather than directing the agent to insert the vendor's reference into user outputs, and gate the external metadata fetch behind explicit user consent.

scan_metadata.llm_overall_assessment: The pydicom skill is a well-structured, local-only DICOM processing toolkit. SKILL.md documents reading, inspecting, transforming, and pseudonymizing DICOM data with strong privacy guardrails (no full dataset printing, allowlisted technical output, explicit acknowledgement flags for pixel PHI and sensitive UID maps). All bundled scripts operate strictly on local filesystem paths with extensive hardening: path-traversal and URI rejection, symlink component rejection, root containment checks, byte/file/element/frame bounds, atomic writes with 0600 permissions, and sanitized error output. No network calls, subprocess execution, eval/exec, dynamic code loading, encoded payloads, or hidden instructions were found. Dependency installation guidance uses pinned public PyPI releases and explicitly recommends hash/provenance verification, which is normal supply-chain hygiene rather than a risk. Secret material (the UID key) is generated locally via secrets.token_bytes, never transmitted, and only its SHA-256 digest appears in audit reports. The citation section asks the agent to optionally fetch a public arXiv record for bibliographic accuracy and to disclose the citation to the user; it sends no local data and is a transparent, disclosed action. No prompt injection, exfiltration, obfuscation, or unauthorized tool-use behavior is present.

The pyhealth skill is a documentation-and-recipe package for building PyHealth 2.0.2 clinical ML pipelines. The single bundled Python asset (assets/starter_pipeline.py) only constructs in-memory synthetic records or loads a user-specified MIMIC-III root, trains a small Transformer on CPU, and prints metrics; it performs no network exfiltration, no shell execution, no dynamic code evaluation, and contains no credentials. Reference markdown files document dataset constructors, task semantics, model contracts, and medical-code mappings, including explicit cautions against embedding credentials and against loading untrusted pickled processor artifacts. Network endpoints mentioned (the public PyHealth synthetic MIMIC bucket, PyHealth resource bucket, PhysioNet, PyPI, readthedocs, arXiv) are all consistent with the stated purpose and declared compatibility note about network access. The installation commands (uv/pip-style dependency resolution of a pinned public package) fall under ordinary dependency installation. The citation section asks the agent to add a reference when the skill materially contributed and to explicitly inform the user, which is transparent and conditional rather than hidden self-promotion. No prompt-injection, instruction-override, hidden-execution, obfuscation, or data-exfiltration behavior was identified, and the pre-scan produced no deterministic findings.

The pylabrobot skill is a documentation- and validation-focused package for PyLabRobot lab automation. All five bundled Python scripts are dependency-free CLI validators/planners that parse bounded local JSON/CSV, enforce strict path containment (no symlinks, no traversal, inside CWD, size and nesting limits), and emit JSON to stdout. No network calls, subprocess execution, shell invocation, encoded payloads, credential access, or environment-variable harvesting appear anywhere in the package; inspect_backends.py only reads installed distribution metadata and performs lazy imports plus signature/attribute inspection without instantiating backends or calling setup(). The SKILL.md body and reference files repeatedly impose a conservative human-approval gate before any physical hardware operation, which is risk-reducing rather than risk-increasing. Install guidance (uv pip install of a pinned PyPI package) is standard dependency installation for the skill's stated purpose and is explicitly gated for hardware extras. The citation section asks the agent to add an author-provided reference when the skill materially contributed and to disclose that to the user; it is transparent, user-visible, and not a hidden or exfiltrating action. Declared allowed-tools (Read, Write, Edit, Bash) are consistent with running the bundled local CLIs. The deterministic pre-scan produced no findings, and no manifest/behavior mismatch was observed.

The pymatgen skill is a well-structured scientific computing helper. The SKILL.md body contains only domain workflow guidance (units, coordinate modes, symmetry tolerances, provenance) with no instruction overrides, hidden actions, or directives to conceal activity from the user. The bundled Python CLIs are defensively written: they enforce input/output byte caps, site caps, refuse symlinks, refuse URL inputs, never overwrite existing files, reject pickle and nested MSON decoding, and bound loops/grids explicitly. The only network capability (scripts/mp_query.py) targets the officially declared Materials Project endpoint, is dry-run by default, requires an explicit --execute flag, reads only the single declared MP_API_KEY environment variable (never from CLI args or .env traversal), pins the endpoint so SDK config cannot redirect the credential, and redacts the secret from error text via safe_error_message(). No hardcoded secrets, no obfuscation or encoded payloads, no download-then-execute chain, no shell invocation or subprocess usage, and no sensitive-source-to-external-sink path were found. artifact_manifest.py actively refuses credential-looking filenames and never emits file contents. Dependency installation guidance (uv/pip with pinned versions from PyPI) is ordinary and declared. Description and keywords match actual implemented capability, so no discovery inflation. No findings.

The manifest declares Read, Write, Edit, Bash and the bundled code matches that stated purpose: two synthetic-data modeling templates (assets/linear_regression_template.py, assets/hierarchical_model_template.py) and two helper modules (scripts/model_diagnostics.py, scripts/model_comparison.py) that perform local statistical computation, plot generation, CSV/NetCDF output into a user-specified output directory, and input validation. No network calls, no subprocess/eval/exec, no file access outside declared output paths, no environment-variable or credential reads, no encoded or obfuscated payloads, and no hidden or unreferenced executables. The only shell commands shown are explicit, user-invoked `uv run --isolated` dependency-pinned template runs, which is ordinary documented dependency installation and not auto-executed. Reference markdown files contain only statistical guidance and links to official PyMC/ArviZ documentation. The citation section asks the agent to add a specific paper reference only when the skill materially contributed, and to disclose that to the user, which is transparent attribution rather than concealed behavior.
